metadata.description: Curated sample of quantum computing papers from academic institutions, commercial companies, and independent groups.
provenance: This is a hand-curated teaching dataset, not a complete bibliography.
Bibliographic fields were compiled by the project author from the published record and MUST be checked against the linked DOI or arXiv identifier before being cited in your own work.
Citation counts are deliberately omitted. They change over time and reporting them accurately would require a live bibliographic source.
The `difficulty` and `hardware_platform` fields are editorial classifications, not claims made by the paper.
metadata.author_list_policy: Only author lists reproduced from the published record are included. Where the full list is very long, a leading-author prefix is given and `authors_truncated` is set to true.

papers.title: Quantum Computing in the NISQ Era and Beyond
papers.abstract: Noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices are expected to become available in the near future. They will have 50 to 100 qubits, gate errors of order 1e-3, and cannot be fault tolerant. This paper surveys the algorithmic opportunities and obstacles for NISQ technology, including the need for error mitigation and for algorithms whose success does not depend on the asymptotic scaling of quantum advantage.

papers.title: Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
papers.abstract: A quantum algorithm is introduced that produces approximate solutions to combinatorial optimisation problems. The circuit has depth p and depends on 2p classical parameters. The expected fraction of optimal solutions is at least 0.684 at p=1, and the approximation quality improves as p increases. The circuit can be simulated classically with resources scaling polynomially in the number of qubits, which bounds the speedup for shallow p.

papers.title: A Fast Quantum Mechanical Algorithm for Database Search
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 28th Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing
papers.abstract: A new quantum mechanical algorithm searches an unsorted database of N entries in O(sqrt(N)) time, using a sequence of unitary transformations and an amplitude amplification step. The algorithm needs only about sqrt(N) iterations, giving a quadratic improvement over the best classical search, and it works for any number of marked entries.

papers.title: Algorithms for Quantum Computation: Discrete Logarithms and Factoring
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 35th Annual Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science
papers.abstract: A quantum mechanical algorithm is given for computing discrete logarithms and for factoring integers. Both problems are solved in time polynomial in the logarithm of the input, using a quantum Fourier transform of period functions. Factoring reduces to finding the order of a group element, which a coherent quantum computer can do in time polynomial in the logarithm of N.

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Algorithms for Prime Factorization and Discrete Logarithms on a Quantum Computer
papers.abstract: A quantum algorithm is presented for factoring N in time O((log N)^3) and for computing discrete logarithms in a similar time bound, both improving on the best known classical algorithms. The algorithm uses the quantum Fourier transform to find the period of a multiplicative sequence, and continued fractions to extract the period from a measured probability distribution.

papers.title: Good Quantum Error-Correcting Codes for Weight t and Large Distance
papers.abstract: An explicit family of quantum error-correcting codes is constructed, built from classical codes, that corrects t errors at block length scaling as the square of 1/(p-1) where p is the parity-check matrix density of the classical code. The construction gives distance proportional to block length and supports a threshold result for local stochastic noise.

papers.title: Surface Codes: Towards Practical Large-Scale Quantum Computation
papers.organisation: Google and University of California, Santa Barbara
papers.abstract: The surface code is presented as a two-dimensional topological code whose stabilisers require only nearest-neighbour interactions. Its threshold is computed to be about 1 percent for independent bit and phase flip errors, and the required physical error rate for a given target logical error rate is given by an explicit formula. Overhead estimates for surface-code-encoded logical qubits are derived.

papers.title: Quantum Computing in the Presence of Noise
papers.abstract: A fault-tolerant quantum computer is modelled as a probabilistic computer that can be simulated by a classical machine if the error rate per gate is below a critical threshold. The analysis gives an explicit threshold and an overhead polynomial in the accuracy required, establishing that arbitrarily long computations are possible below threshold.

papers.title: Quantum Linear Systems of Equations
papers.abstract: A quantum algorithm solves a sparse system of linear equations in time O(polylog N), exponentially faster than the best known classical algorithm. The algorithm uses quantum phase estimation and Hamiltonian simulation, and the output is the state of a solution vector rather than an explicit readable vector. Conditions are given under which the output can be efficiently verified.

papers.title: Quantum Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Quantum machine learning concerns using quantum computers to learn from data. The paper reviews the quantum analogs of classical machine learning primitives, including kernel methods, quantum perceptrons, quantum Boltzmann machines and quantum state discrimination, and discusses which tasks admit an advantage under specific data-loading assumptions.

papers.title: Zero-Noise Extrapolation for Error Mitigation of Noisy Gates in Quantum Circuits
papers.abstract: A method is presented for estimating the error-mitigated expectation value of an observable by computing it on deliberately noisier circuits. The noisier circuits are obtained by inserting additional noisy identity gates. The expectation value is a smooth polynomial function of the noise strength, and a quadratic or cubic fit is extrapolated to zero noise. Results on a superconducting device show a reduction in bias without exponential sampling cost.

papers.title: Error Mitigation with Clifford Data Regression
papers.abstract: A scalable error mitigation technique is introduced that uses a classical linear-regression model fitted to a small number of low-noise Clifford circuits, and applied to high-noise non-Clifford circuits. The method reduces the sampling overhead substantially compared with zero-noise extrapolation and does not require an exponential fit in circuit depth.

papers.title: Experimental Realization of a Compiled Variational Quantum Eigensolver
papers.abstract: A two-qubit superconducting processor computes the ground-state energy of the H2 molecule and of BeH2 using a compiled variational eigensolver with symmetry tapering. The experimentally measured energies agree with exact diagonalisation within tens of millihartree after error mitigation.

papers.title: Quantum Supremacy Using a Programmable Superconducting Processor
papers.abstract: A programmable superconducting processor with 53 usable qubits is used to sample from the output distribution of a benchmark random quantum circuit. The processor requires about 200 seconds to sample one instance a million times; the equivalent task on a state-of-the-art classical supercomputer would take roughly 10,000 years. The result is verified by a classical simulation and by a set of increasingly demanding instant-classical algorithms.

papers.title: Practical Quantum Computing with Superconducting Circuits
papers.abstract: A review of superconducting qubits as a platform for quantum computing, covering the transmon design, dispersive readout, the coherence times, and the strategies used to extend them. The review closes with the requirements for scalable error correction and a comparison of coherence-limited and leakage-limited regimes.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Trapped-Ion Hyperfine Qubits
papers.organisation: National Institute of Standards and Technology
papers.abstract: A review of the use of trapped ions as qubits, covering state preparation, single-qubit and two-qubit gates, and state detection. The review discusses motional decoherence, the Doppler and micromotion limits on gate speed, and the scaling of Coulomb repulsion to large ion chains.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Neutral Atoms
papers.abstract: Neutral atoms held in optical tweezers are reviewed as a platform for quantum information processing. The review covers Rydberg-mediated two-qubit gates, the resulting blockade interaction, single-atom loading and detection, and the prospects for scaling to thousands of qubits in two-dimensional arrays.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Photonic States
papers.abstract: A scheme for universal quantum computation with linear optics, single photons, and photodetection is described. Despite photons not interacting directly, a measurement-induced nonlinearity and ancilla photons suffice to implement a universal gate set, at the cost of probabilistic post-selection.

papers.title: Quantum Computing with Topological Qubits
papers.abstract: A review of proposals for encoding quantum information in non-Abelian anyons, which are intrinsically immune to local errors. The review covers the toric code and its generalisations, the Kitaev honeycomb model, the non-Abelian quantum Hall state, and braiding operations for topologically protected gates.

papers.title: Quantum Simulation of Many-Body Systems
papers.abstract: Digital and analog quantum simulation of strongly correlated quantum systems is reviewed. Digital simulation encodes the problem in qubits using a fermionic or bosonic mapping and evolves the Hamiltonian with gate sequences; analog simulation evolves an engineered Hamiltonian directly. Applications to condensed matter, high-energy physics and quantum chemistry are surveyed.

papers.title: Quantum Communication in the Presence of Decoherence
papers.abstract: The capacity of a quantum channel in the presence of decoherence is studied, and the hashing inequality is used to bound how much noiseless quantum communication can be extracted from a noisy link. The result gives the threshold of a concatenated repetition code below which reliable communication is possible.

papers.title: Element Distinctness with Quantum Queries
papers.abstract: A lower bound is proved showing that a bounded-error quantum algorithm for the element distinctness problem requires at least Omega(N^(5/7)) queries, and a quantum walk algorithm is given matching that bound up to a constant factor. The result improves the earlier Omega(N^(2/3)) lower bound and settles the query complexity.

papers.title: Quantum Volume in Practice
papers.abstract: A method is described for assigning a single figure of merit to a quantum processor based on the largest square circuit it can execute successfully, with heavy-tailed output distributions used to separate genuine quantum behaviour from classical simulation. The method is applied to report the quantum volume of several devices.

papers.title: Quantum Advantage in Learning from Experiments
papers.abstract: A programmable superconducting processor is used as a physical simulator for learning a low-dimensional hypothesis class from experimental observations. The number of experiments required is independent of the Hilbert-space dimension, and the protocol is validated on a seven-qubit device.

papers.title: Probabilistic Error Cancellation for Quantum Measurement
papers.abstract: A measurement-error mitigation method is derived that requires only a single measurement bit for a single-qubit readout, using a probabilistic error cancellation scheme. The method is compared against linear inversion and exponential-noise-cancellation methods, and the sampling cost is shown to scale polynomially in the error probability.
